structures.name: Horizontal fissure (right)
structures.note: Between the right upper and middle lobes; often incomplete.

structures.name: Oblique fissure (right)
structures.note: Between the lower lobe and the upper and middle lobes.

structures.name: Oblique fissure (left)
structures.note: Where the upper and lower lobe segmentations meet. Real fissures are often incomplete; this shows the plane, not its completeness.

structures.name: Upper lobe veins (superior vein, upper trunk)
Left phrenic nerve
structures.note: Schematic, drawn on landmarks: crosses the arch anterolaterally and runs on the pericardium anterior to the hilum with the pericardiophrenic vessels.

structures.name: Left vagus nerve
structures.note: Schematic: crosses the arch posterior to the phrenic nerve, gives the recurrent laryngeal nerve at the arch, then passes behind the hilum onto the esophagus.

structures.name: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve
structures.note: Schematic: hooks under the arch lateral to the ligamentum arteriosum and climbs in the tracheo-esophageal groove. At risk clearing station 5.

structures.name: Ligamentum arteriosum
structures.note: Schematic: from the top of the left PA to the underside of the arch. The recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around it.

structures.name: Inferior pulmonary ligament
structures.note: Schematic: the pleural fold below the inferior pulmonary vein, divided first in a lower lobectomy. Station 9 nodes lie in it.

structures.name: Station 5 (subaortic, AP window)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 6 (para-aortic)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 7 (subcarinal)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 10L (hilar)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 11L (interlobar)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 9L (pulmonary ligament)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Azygos vein (arch)
structures.note: Schematic: ascends on the right of the vertebral bodies and arches forward over the right main bronchus into the back of the SVC.

structures.name: Right phrenic nerve
structures.note: Schematic: on the lateral surface of the SVC, then the pericardium anterior to the hilum.

structures.name: Right vagus nerve
structures.note: Schematic: descends on the right of the trachea, passes medial to the azygos arch and behind the hilum onto the esophagus.

structures.name: Inferior pulmonary ligament (right)
structures.note: Schematic: the pleural fold below the right inferior pulmonary vein, divided first in a lower lobectomy. Station 9R nodes lie in it.

structures.name: Station 4R (lower paratracheal)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 10R (hilar)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 11R (interlobar)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Station 9R (pulmonary ligament)
structures.note: Schematic node station placed on landmarks (IASLC map).

structures.name: Posterolateral thoracotomy incision (5th space)
structures.note: Schematic: from the anterior axillary line, curving below the tip of the scapula; latissimus dorsi divided, serratus anterior spared, chest entered over the 6th rib.

structures.name: Posterolateral thoracotomy incision (5th space)
structures.note: Schematic: from the anterior axillary line, curving below the tip of the scapula; latissimus dorsi divided, serratus anterior spared, chest entered over the 6th rib.

structures.name: Anterolateral thoracotomy incision (5th space)
structures.note: Schematic: along the 5th intercostal space (below the nipple, in the inframammary fold in women), from the sternal edge to the mid-axillary line.

structures.name: Anterolateral thoracotomy incision (5th space)
structures.note: Schematic: along the 5th intercostal space (below the nipple, in the inframammary fold in women), from the sternal edge to the mid-axillary line.

structures.name: Clamshell incision (bilateral anterolateral + transverse sternotomy)
structures.note: Schematic: both 5th-space anterolateral incisions joined across the sternum.

structures.name: Left internal mammary artery
structures.note: Schematic: descends behind the costal cartilages 1-2 cm from the sternal edge. Divided by a clamshell; ligate both ends once there is a circulation.

structures.name: Right internal mammary artery
structures.note: Schematic: descends behind the costal cartilages 1-2 cm from the sternal edge. Divided by a clamshell; ligate both ends once there is a circulation.

structures.name: Pericardiotomy line
structures.note: Opened longitudinally, anterior to and parallel with the phrenic nerve, from the base to the apex.

structures.name: Stab wound, right ventricle
structures.note: Teaching example of a ventricular stab wound.

structures.name: Missile tract, left lower lobe
structures.note: Teaching example: a bleeding through-and-through tract away from the hilum, treated by tractotomy.

structures.name: Serratus anterior, left
structures.note: Schematic, on this patient's ribs. Digitations from ribs 1 to 8, passing deep to the scapula to its medial border. Spared in a muscle-sparing thoracotomy; the long thoracic nerve runs on its surface.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi, left
structures.note: Schematic. From T7-T12, the thoracolumbar fascia and the lower ribs, over the scapular tip to the humerus. Divided in a standard posterolateral thoracotomy; retracted in a muscle-sparing one.

structures.name: Trapezius (lower fibres), left
structures.note: Schematic. Divided only when a posterolateral incision is carried up between the scapula and the spine.

structures.name: Rhomboids, left
structures.note: Schematic. Deep to trapezius, spine to the medial border of the scapula.

structures.name: Pectoralis major, left
structures.note: Schematic. Its lateral border is the anterior axillary fold; anterolateral incisions and anterior ports pass at or below it.

structures.name: Intercostal muscles, left
structures.note: Schematic. External, internal and innermost layers between the ribs; divided on the upper border of the lower rib to spare the neurovascular bundle.

structures.name: Long thoracic nerve, left
structures.note: Schematic. On the outer surface of serratus anterior in the mid-axillary line: injury gives a winged scapula.

structures.name: Thoracodorsal nerve and vessels, left
structures.note: Schematic. On the deep surface of latissimus dorsi near its anterior border: kept in a muscle-sparing thoracotomy.

structures.name: Anterior axillary line, left
structures.note: Surface landmark, drawn on the skin.

structures.name: Mid-axillary line, left
structures.note: Surface landmark, drawn on the skin.

structures.name: Posterior axillary line, left
structures.note: Surface landmark, drawn on the skin.

structures.name: Tip of the scapula, left
structures.note: Inferior angle of the scapula: about the 7th rib / 7th space with the arm by the side. The posterolateral incision passes 2-3 cm below it.

structures.name: Nipple (4th space, male), left
structures.note: In a man the nipple lies over the 4th intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line; not a reliable landmark in a woman.

structures.name: Uniportal incision, 4th space
structures.note: Single 3-4 cm incision in the 4th space between the anterior and mid-axillary lines: upper lobes. Camera at the back of the wound, instruments below it.

structures.name: Uniportal incision, 5th space
structures.note: Single 3-4 cm incision in the 5th space between the anterior and mid-axillary lines: middle and lower lobes.

structures.name: Biportal utility incision, 4th space
structures.note: Two-port VATS: a 3-4 cm utility incision in the 4th (upper lobes) or 5th space at the anterior axillary line.

structures.name: Biportal camera port, 7th space
structures.note: Two-port VATS: 1 cm camera port in the 7th (or 8th) space in the mid- to posterior axillary line.

structures.name: Muscle-sparing lateral thoracotomy incision
structures.note: Schematic: vertical, 10-12 cm, along the anterior border of latissimus dorsi, from the axilla down; flaps raised, latissimus retracted back, serratus retracted forward or split.

structures.name: Serratus anterior, right
structures.note: Schematic, on this patient's ribs. Digitations from ribs 1 to 8, passing deep to the scapula to its medial border. Spared in a muscle-sparing thoracotomy; the long thoracic nerve runs on its surface.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi, right
structures.note: Schematic. From T7-T12, the thoracolumbar fascia and the lower ribs, over the scapular tip to the humerus. Divided in a standard posterolateral thoracotomy; retracted in a muscle-sparing one.

structures.name: Trapezius (lower fibres), right
structures.note: Schematic. Divided only when a posterolateral incision is carried up between the scapula and the spine.

structures.name: Rhomboids, right
structures.note: Schematic. Deep to trapezius, spine to the medial border of the scapula.

structures.name: Pectoralis major, right
structures.note: Schematic. Its lateral border is the anterior axillary fold; anterolateral incisions and anterior ports pass at or below it.

structures.name: Intercostal muscles, right
structures.note: Schematic. External, internal and innermost layers between the ribs; divided on the upper border of the lower rib to spare the neurovascular bundle.

structures.name: Long thoracic nerve, right
structures.note: Schematic. On the outer surface of serratus anterior in the mid-axillary line: injury gives a winged scapula.

structures.name: Thoracodorsal nerve and vessels, right
structures.note: Schematic. On the deep surface of latissimus dorsi near its anterior border: kept in a muscle-sparing thoracotomy.

structures.name: Anterior axillary line, right
structures.note: Surface landmark, drawn on the skin.

structures.name: Mid-axillary line, right
structures.note: Surface landmark, drawn on the skin.

structures.name: Posterior axillary line, right
structures.note: Surface landmark, drawn on the skin.

structures.name: Tip of the scapula, right
structures.note: Inferior angle of the scapula: about the 7th rib / 7th space with the arm by the side. The posterolateral incision passes 2-3 cm below it.

structures.name: Nipple (4th space, male), right
structures.note: In a man the nipple lies over the 4th intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line; not a reliable landmark in a woman.

structures.name: Uniportal incision, 4th space
structures.note: Single 3-4 cm incision in the 4th space between the anterior and mid-axillary lines: upper lobes. Camera at the back of the wound, instruments below it.

structures.name: Uniportal incision, 5th space
structures.note: Single 3-4 cm incision in the 5th space between the anterior and mid-axillary lines: middle and lower lobes.

structures.name: Biportal utility incision, 4th space
structures.note: Two-port VATS: a 3-4 cm utility incision in the 4th (upper lobes) or 5th space at the anterior axillary line.

structures.name: Biportal camera port, 7th space
structures.note: Two-port VATS: 1 cm camera port in the 7th (or 8th) space in the mid- to posterior axillary line.

structures.name: Muscle-sparing lateral thoracotomy incision
structures.note: Schematic: vertical, 10-12 cm, along the anterior border of latissimus dorsi, from the axilla down; flaps raised, latissimus retracted back, serratus retracted forward or split.

structures.name: Thymus and anterior mediastinal fat
structures.note: The fat of the anterior mediastinum between the great vessels and the sternum, from the thyroid to the pericardium: in an adult the involuted thymus lies in it, and an extended thymectomy removes all of it from phrenic nerve to phrenic nerve.

structures.name: Thymic vein 1
structures.note: Schematic: one to three thymic veins leave the back of the gland and drain into the left brachiocephalic (innominate) vein; tie or clip them before lifting the gland off it.

structures.name: Thymic vein 2
structures.note: Schematic: one to three thymic veins leave the back of the gland and drain into the left brachiocephalic (innominate) vein; tie or clip them before lifting the gland off it.

structures.name: Gastric conduit (to the apex of the chest)
structures.note: Schematic: the tubularised greater curvature, 4-5 cm wide, pulled up the esophageal bed to above the azygos arch (Ivor Lewis).

structures.name: Gastric conduit (to the neck)
structures.note: Schematic: the conduit through the posterior mediastinum to the left neck (McKeown, transhiatal).

structures.name: Intrathoracic anastomosis (Ivor Lewis)
structures.note: Schematic: circular stapled (intrathoracic) or hand-sewn / linear-stapled (neck).

structures.name: Cervical anastomosis
structures.note: Schematic: circular stapled (intrathoracic) or hand-sewn / linear-stapled (neck).

structures.name: Left gastric artery (from the coeliac trunk)
structures.note: Schematic: the coeliac trunk leaves the front of the aorta at T12-L1; the left gastric artery runs up to the lesser curvature. Divided at its origin with the coeliac nodes; the conduit lives on the right gastroepiploic artery.

structures.name: Right gastroepiploic artery (greater curvature arcade)
structures.note: Schematic: the arcade along the greater curvature that the conduit lives on. Keep 1-2 cm away from it when dividing the omentum and short gastrics.

structures.name: Upper midline laparotomy
structures.note: Schematic: xiphoid to umbilicus. For the abdominal phase of an esophagectomy (or a roof-top incision; or laparoscopy).

structures.name: Left neck incision (anterior border of sternocleidomastoid)
structures.note: Schematic: along the anterior border of the left sternocleidomastoid, from the sternal notch up. The carotid sheath goes laterally; the left recurrent laryngeal nerve lies in the tracheo-esophageal groove: no metal retractor on it.

structures.name: Thoracic duct
structures.note: Schematic: from the cisterna chyli (L1-L2) through the aortic hiatus, up between the aorta and the azygos on the right of the vertebral bodies, crossing to the left behind the esophagus at T4-T6, then up on the left of the esophagus to the left venous angle. Variants (double, plexiform) are common.

structures.name: Cisterna chyli
structures.note: Schematic: the sac at L1-L2, behind and to the right of the aorta, deep to the right crus.

structures.name: Visceral peel (fibrous cortex), left
structures.note: Schematic: the organised fibrinous cortex on the visceral pleura that traps the lung in a stage III (chronic) empyema. Decortication peels it off so the lung re-expands.

structures.name: Empyema collection (posterior, basal), left
structures.note: Schematic: loculated pus in the posterior costophrenic gutter, where it collects in a supine patient. Drawn in the pleural space of this scan, which is itself normal.

structures.name: Post-intubation tracheal stenosis
structures.note: Teaching example: a 2 cm cuff-level stricture, 2 cm below the cricoid. Resected as a sleeve.

structures.name: Trachea above the stenosis (to the cricoid)
structures.note: Schematic from the CT centreline; carried up to the cricoid, just above this scan.

structures.name: Trachea below the stenosis
structures.note: Schematic from the CT centreline.

structures.name: Cricoid cartilage
structures.note: Schematic, above this scan: the only complete ring of the airway.

structures.name: Thyroid cartilage
structures.note: Schematic, above this scan: the two laminae meet in front at the laryngeal prominence.

structures.name: Tracheal blood supply (lateral, segmental)
structures.note: Schematic: small segmental branches (mostly from the inferior thyroid artery) enter the trachea laterally. Free the trachea circumferentially only for about 1 cm beyond each cut.

structures.name: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve (neck)
structures.note: Schematic: up from under the aortic arch in the left tracheo-esophageal groove, entering the larynx behind the cricothyroid joint.

structures.name: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve (neck)
structures.note: Schematic: loops under the right subclavian artery and runs up obliquely toward the right tracheo-esophageal groove; more lateral low in the neck than the left.

structures.name: External branch, superior laryngeal nerve (left)
structures.note: Schematic: close to the superior thyroid artery near the upper pole, down on the inferior constrictor to cricothyroid. Injury: a weak, low-pitched voice that tires.

structures.name: Internal branch, superior laryngeal nerve (left)
structures.note: Schematic: pierces the thyrohyoid membrane (sensation above the cords). At risk in a thyrohyoid laryngeal release: aspiration.

structures.name: External branch, superior laryngeal nerve (right)
structures.note: Schematic: close to the superior thyroid artery near the upper pole, down on the inferior constrictor to cricothyroid. Injury: a weak, low-pitched voice that tires.

structures.name: Internal branch, superior laryngeal nerve (right)
structures.note: Schematic: pierces the thyrohyoid membrane (sensation above the cords). At risk in a thyrohyoid laryngeal release: aspiration.

structures.name: Platysma
structures.note: Schematic: raised with the skin as subplatysmal flaps, up to the thyroid cartilage and down to the notch.

structures.name: Strap muscles (left: sternohyoid, sternothyroid)
structures.note: Schematic: separated in the midline (the avascular linea alba of the neck) and retracted laterally.

structures.name: Strap muscles (right: sternohyoid, sternothyroid)
structures.note: Schematic: separated in the midline (the avascular linea alba of the neck) and retracted laterally.

structures.name: Collar incision
structures.note: Low collar incision, two fingerbreadths above the sternal notch; an old stoma is included in it.

structures.name: Lateral stay sutures (2-0)
structures.note: Traction sutures through the full wall laterally, a ring beyond each cut: they hold the ends, test the tension, and are crossed and held while the anastomosis is tied.

structures.name: Cross-field endotracheal tube
structures.note: A sterile armoured tube passed into the distal trachea across the field and connected to a sterile circuit; out for short periods while the sutures are placed.

structures.name: Orotracheal tube (advanced across the anastomosis)
structures.note: Advanced from above past the anastomosis before the anterior sutures are tied.

structures.name: Coronary arteries (segmented)
structures.note: From the CT; small vessels are incomplete on this scan.

structures.name: Mitral annulus
structures.note: The LA-LV junction on this scan, fitted to a ring. Anteriorly it is continuous with the aortic valve (aortomitral curtain).

structures.name: Anterior mitral leaflet
structures.note: Schematic: the larger, anterior leaflet, in continuity with the aortic valve.

structures.name: Posterior mitral leaflet
structures.note: Schematic: the posterior (mural) leaflet, P1-P3; its chordae are kept in a chordal-sparing replacement.

structures.name: Papillary muscles (anterolateral, posteromedial)
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: Chordae tendineae
structures.note: Schematic: from the papillary muscles to both leaflets.

structures.name: Coronary sinus
structures.note: Schematic: in the posterior AV groove, about 1 cm on the atrial side of the posterior annulus, opening into the right atrium. Retrograde cardioplegia goes in here.

structures.name: Circumflex artery (AV groove)
structures.note: Schematic: close to the posterior annulus near the anterolateral commissure, especially if left-dominant. A deep suture there can catch it.

structures.name: AV node region (Koch's triangle)
structures.note: Schematic: near the posteromedial commissure and the right fibrous trigone. Deep bites here cause heart block.

structures.name: Left atriotomy (Sondergaard's groove)
structures.note: Through the interatrial groove, in front of the right pulmonary veins, after developing Sondergaard's plane.

structures.name: Transseptal incision (through the fossa ovalis)
structures.note: Vertical incision through the fossa ovalis, extended up if needed (the superior septal approach carries it across the dome of the LA).

structures.name: Right atriotomy
structures.note: Oblique, from the appendage toward the IVC, parallel to the AV groove (away from the sinus node at the SVC junction).

structures.name: Aortic cannula
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: SVC cannula
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: IVC cannula (tip in the IVC)
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: Antegrade cardioplegia needle (aortic root)
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: Retrograde cardioplegia cannula (coronary sinus)
structures.note: Schematic: passed through a purse-string in the right atrium into the coronary sinus.

structures.name: Tricuspid annulus
structures.note: The RA-RV junction on this scan. In functional TR it dilates mainly along the anterior and posterior leaflets; the septal part is fixed by the fibrous skeleton.

structures.name: Septal leaflet (tricuspid)
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: Anterior leaflet (tricuspid)
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: Posterior leaflet (tricuspid)
structures.note: Schematic.

structures.name: Koch's triangle
structures.note: Bounded by the coronary sinus ostium, the tendon of Todaro and the septal leaflet hinge. The AV node lies at its apex, near the anteroseptal commissure: no deep bites there.

structures.name: AV node and His bundle (apex of Koch's triangle)
Right coronary artery (right AV groove)
structures.note: Schematic: a few millimetres outside the anterior and posterior annulus, closest near the anteroposterior commissure. Deep bites or a downsized rigid ring can kink it.

structures.name: Incomplete annuloplasty ring
structures.note: Schematic: open at the anteroseptal commissure and the AV node; it reshapes and reduces the anterior and posterior annulus.

structures.name: De Vega suture annuloplasty (double running)
structures.note: Schematic: two parallel running polypropylene sutures from the anteroseptal to the posteroseptal commissure, tied over pledgets to shorten the anterior and posterior annulus.

structures.name: Stented bioprosthesis, tricuspid (~32 mm)
structures.note: Schematic: posts at the commissures, none pointing into the right ventricular outflow tract.

structures.name: Caval snares (SVC and IVC)
structures.note: Tapes round both cavae, tightened over the cannulas so that the right atrium can be opened without air entering the venous line.

structures.name: Mechanical bileaflet prosthesis (~29 mm)
structures.note: Schematic: a bileaflet valve on its sewing ring, seated on the annulus.

structures.name: Right mini-thoracotomy (4th space)
structures.note: 4-6 cm in the right 4th space, in the inframammary fold, anterior to the anterior axillary line.

structures.name: Aortic annulus (crown-shaped hinge line)
structures.note: The cusps hinge on a three-pronged crown: low at each nadir (the virtual basal ring), high at the commissures just below the sinotubular junction. Sutures follow this line.

structures.name: Right coronary cusp (leaflet)
structures.note: Schematic, thickened and calcified as in degenerative or rheumatic stenosis.

structures.name: Left coronary cusp (leaflet)
structures.note: Schematic, thickened and calcified as in degenerative or rheumatic stenosis.

structures.name: Non-coronary cusp (leaflet)
structures.note: Schematic, thickened and calcified as in degenerative or rheumatic stenosis.

structures.name: Calcium on the cusps and annulus
structures.note: Schematic: nodular calcium on the cusps, extending into the annulus at the nadirs. Debride it all, catching every fragment.

structures.name: Right coronary ostium
structures.note: About 1-1.5 cm above the annulus in its sinus. Keep prosthesis posts and pledgets clear of it, and look into it before closing.

structures.name: Left main coronary ostium
structures.note: About 1-1.5 cm above the annulus in its sinus. Keep prosthesis posts and pledgets clear of it, and look into it before closing.

structures.name: Membranous septum and His bundle
structures.note: Below the commissure between the right and non-coronary cusps. Deep bites or aggressive debridement here cause complete heart block.

structures.name: Aortotomy (oblique, into the non-coronary sinus)
structures.note: Oblique ("hockey-stick"): across the front of the aorta 1-1.5 cm above the right coronary, then down into the non-coronary sinus toward its nadir. Stay above the right coronary ostium.

structures.name: Stented bioprosthesis (~22 mm)
structures.note: Schematic: sewing ring on the annulus, three posts at the native commissures so none faces a coronary ostium.

structures.name: Two-stage venous cannula (RA appendage to IVC)
structures.note: Schematic: through a purse-string in the right atrial appendage, the tip in the IVC, the side holes in the atrium.

structures.name: LV vent (right superior pulmonary vein)
structures.note: Schematic: through the right superior pulmonary vein, across the mitral valve into the LV. Keeps the arrested ventricle empty, above all with aortic regurgitation.

structures.name: Hand-held ostial cardioplegia cannulas
structures.note: Schematic: soft-tipped cannulas held in the left main and right coronary ostia once the aorta is open.

structures.name: Upper hemisternotomy (J into the right 3rd/4th space)
structures.note: From the sternal notch down the midline to the 3rd or 4th space, then out to the right. The lower sternum stays whole; watch the right internal thoracic vessels at the J.

structures.name: Skin incision for upper hemisternotomy (about 6-8 cm)
Right anterior mini-thoracotomy (2nd space)
structures.note: 5-6 cm in the right 2nd space from the sternal edge; the right internal thoracic vessels ligated or kept, the 3rd costal cartilage divided if more room is needed.

structures.name: Aortic root aneurysm (schematic, ~55 mm at the sinuses)
structures.note: Schematic: sinuses of Valsalva dilated, effacing the sinotubular junction. The CT root itself is normal size.

structures.name: Left main button
structures.note: A 5-8 mm cuff of sinus wall round the ostium, mobilised just enough to reach the graft without tension.

structures.name: Left main button, reimplanted
structures.note: Sewn end-to-side to a hole in the graft with running 5-0 polypropylene. The right button is placed with the heart filled, to avoid kinking.

structures.name: Right coronary button
structures.note: A 5-8 mm cuff of sinus wall round the ostium, mobilised just enough to reach the graft without tension.

structures.name: Right coronary button, reimplanted
structures.note: Sewn end-to-side to a hole in the graft with running 5-0 polypropylene. The right button is placed with the heart filled, to avoid kinking.

structures.name: Composite valved graft (~28 mm tube, mechanical valve)
structures.note: Schematic: a crimped polyester graft with the valve sewn into its base (or a tissue valve: a "bio-Bentall").

structures.name: Reimplantation graft (~31 mm), the native valve inside
structures.note: Schematic: a straight or Valsalva-shaped polyester graft, its base below the valve at the ventriculo-aortic junction; the valve is sewn inside it.

structures.name: Subannular sutures (horizontal mattress, inside out)
structures.note: A single horizontal plane just below the nadirs of the cusps, passed from inside the LVOT out through the base of the graft; shallow (or through the fibrous tissue) under the membranous septum.

structures.name: Commissures resuspended inside the graft
structures.note: Each commissure pulled up vertically and fixed to the graft, at a height that lets the cusps coapt well above the annulus.

structures.name: Pulmonary root (the autograft)
structures.note: The pulmonary valve with 3-5 mm of RV muscle below it and the trunk above it, harvested as a whole root.

structures.name: Autograft harvest lines (PA trunk above, RVOT below)
structures.note: Transect the trunk below the bifurcation; open the RVOT 3-5 mm below the valve and free the root off the septum, staying shallow posteriorly.

structures.name: First septal perforator (LAD)
structures.note: Schematic: leaves the LAD and runs into the septum just beneath the posterior RVOT. Deep dissection here during harvest divides it (septal infarction).

structures.name: Pulmonary autograft in the aortic position
structures.note: Sewn to the aortic annulus with interrupted sutures, the coronary buttons reimplanted into its sinuses, then joined to the ascending aorta. Often reinforced (inclusion in a polyester graft, or annular and STJ stabilisation) to prevent dilatation.

structures.name: Pulmonary homograft (RVOT reconstruction)
structures.note: A cryopreserved pulmonary homograft sewn to the RVOT below and the PA trunk above.

structures.name: Left main coronary artery
structures.note: Epicardial course schematic along the grooves of this heart; proximal left system from the CT.

structures.name: Left anterior descending (LAD)
structures.note: Epicardial course schematic along the grooves of this heart; proximal left system from the CT.

structures.name: Circumflex (LCx)
structures.note: Epicardial course schematic along the grooves of this heart; proximal left system from the CT.

structures.name: Right coronary artery (RCA)
structures.note: Epicardial course schematic along the grooves of this heart; proximal left system from the CT.

structures.name: Posterior descending (PDA)
structures.note: Epicardial course schematic along the grooves of this heart; proximal left system from the CT.

structures.name: First diagonal (D1)
structures.note: Schematic branch.

structures.name: Second diagonal (D2)
structures.note: Schematic branch.

structures.name: First obtuse marginal (OM1)
structures.note: Schematic branch.

structures.name: Second obtuse marginal (OM2)
structures.note: Schematic branch.

structures.name: Acute marginal
structures.note: Schematic branch.

structures.name: Proximal LAD stenosis
structures.note: Schematic plaque: a severe (70% or more) stenosis.

structures.name: OM1 stenosis
structures.note: Schematic plaque: a severe (70% or more) stenosis.

structures.name: Mid RCA stenosis
structures.note: Schematic plaque: a severe (70% or more) stenosis.

structures.name: Left internal mammary (thoracic) artery, in situ
structures.note: About 1-2 cm from the sternal edge, on the back of the chest wall, with its two veins; harvested from the subclavian origin to the bifurcation at the 6th space.

structures.name: LIMA to LAD graft (pedicle)
structures.note: The in-situ LIMA, divided distally and brought down, lateral to the pulmonary artery, to the LAD. The best-proven graft.

structures.name: Proximal anastomosis on the ascending aorta
Proximal anastomosis on the ascending aorta
Saphenous vein graft: aorta to OM1
structures.note: Reversed long saphenous vein; the course round the left side of the heart is judged with the heart full.

structures.name: Radial artery graft: aorta to OM1
structures.note: The radial artery (non-dominant arm), proximal end on the aorta; for a target with a severe stenosis.

structures.name: Left anterior mini-thoracotomy (MIDCAB, 4th space)
structures.note: 6-8 cm in the 4th (or 5th) space, from near the sternal edge laterally; the LIMA is taken down under direct vision or thoracoscopically.

structures.name: Saphenous vein graft: aorta to PDA
structures.note: Reversed long saphenous vein round the acute margin to the inferior wall.

structures.name: Off-pump stabiliser (suction pads on the target)
structures.note: Immobilises a few centimetres of epicardium around the target; an intracoronary shunt or snare keeps the field dry.

structures.name: Sterile drapes (sternotomy window)
structures.note: Adhesive-edged drapes leave a window over the sternum, from the notch to below the xiphoid.

structures.name: Pericardium, opened and hitched (cradle)
structures.note: Opened in the midline and hitched to the sternal edges or drapes with stay sutures: the heart sits in a cradle, raised toward the surgeon.

structures.name: Utility incision, anterior, over the hilum (4th space)
Utility incision, in line with the fissure (5th space)
Utility incision, anterior, over the hilum (4th space)
Utility incision, in line with the fissure (5th space)
Rheumatic mitral valve: fused, thickened, fish-mouth orifice
structures.note: Schematic chronic rheumatic mitral stenosis: commissural fusion turns the two leaflets into a funnel that domes into the LV in diastole, with a small fish-mouth orifice (here about 0.9 cm2; normal 4-6 cm2).

structures.name: Thickened, rolled leaflet edges and fused commissures
structures.note: The fused commissures (the ridges running up to the annulus) are what a balloon or a surgical commissurotomy splits.

structures.name: Calcium in the rheumatic mitral valve
structures.note: Commissural calcium is the strongest single predictor of a poor balloon result (Wilkins); heavy calcium pushes toward surgery.

structures.name: Shortened, thickened, fused chordae
structures.note: Subvalvular disease: fused, short chordae tether the leaflet tips; severe subvalvular fusion makes a balloon or a repair less likely to succeed.

structures.name: Mitral stenosis: high-velocity inflow jet (diastole)
structures.note: Diastole: blood forced through the small orifice at high velocity; the gradient rises with flow and with heart rate (shorter diastole).

structures.name: Mitral regurgitation jet (systole)
structures.note: Systole: blood driven back into the LA. With anterior leaflet prolapse the jet points posteriorly, away from the prolapsing leaflet.

structures.name: Anterior leaflet prolapsing into the LA (acute rheumatic MR)
structures.note: Acute rheumatic carditis: inflamed chordae elongate and the anterior leaflet prolapses (Carpentier type II); the annulus dilates (type I).

structures.name: Vegetation (infective endocarditis), about 12 mm
structures.note: On the atrial side of the anterior leaflet, the low-pressure side of the regurgitant jet. 10 mm or more with an embolic event is an indication for urgent surgery (ESC 2023).

structures.name: Left atrial appendage thrombus
structures.note: Stasis in a large, fibrillating left atrium. A contraindication to balloon commissurotomy; removed, and the appendage closed, at surgery.

structures.name: Rheumatic aortic valve: retracted, thickened cusps
structures.note: Fibrosis retracts the cusps so that they no longer meet in the centre (a central regurgitant gap); one commissure is fused. Later, fusion and calcium add stenosis (mixed disease).

structures.name: Aortic regurgitation jet (diastole)
structures.note: Diastole: blood falls back from the aorta into the LV, which must eject it again: volume and pressure overload, a wide pulse pressure and lower diastolic coronary perfusion.

structures.name: Vegetation on the aortic valve
structures.note: On the ventricular side of the cusp. Cusp perforation and acute severe regurgitation follow.

structures.name: Paravalvular (aortic root) abscess
structures.note: In the aortomitral curtain and under the non-coronary sinus: uncontrolled infection. New PR prolongation or heart block means it has reached the conduction tissue. An indication for urgent surgery; radical debridement, then patch or root replacement.

structures.name: Lung carcinoma, LUL (about 2.9 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a spiculated peripheral tumour. Its size, distance from the hilum and any nodes decide the T and N stage and the resection.

structures.name: Lung carcinoma, LLL (about 2.9 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a spiculated peripheral tumour. Its size, distance from the hilum and any nodes decide the T and N stage and the resection.

structures.name: Lung carcinoma, RUL (about 2.9 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a spiculated peripheral tumour. Its size, distance from the hilum and any nodes decide the T and N stage and the resection.

structures.name: Lung carcinoma, RML (about 2.3 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a spiculated peripheral tumour. Its size, distance from the hilum and any nodes decide the T and N stage and the resection.

structures.name: Lung carcinoma, RLL (about 2.9 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a spiculated peripheral tumour. Its size, distance from the hilum and any nodes decide the T and N stage and the resection.

structures.name: Central (hilar) carcinoma, left
structures.note: Schematic: a central tumour at the hilum, involving the main or lobar bronchus and the pulmonary artery: pneumonectomy territory.

structures.name: Central (hilar) carcinoma, right
structures.note: Schematic: a central tumour at the hilum, involving the main or lobar bronchus and the pulmonary artery: pneumonectomy territory.

structures.name: Post-tuberculous cavity (thick wall)
structures.note: Schematic: a healed TB cavity at the apex, its wall thickened, lined by damaged bronchi and fed by enlarged bronchial and intercostal arteries (the source of haemoptysis).

structures.name: Fungal ball (aspergilloma)
structures.note: A mass of Aspergillus hyphae, mucus and debris lying free in the cavity; it moves with posture (the dependent part of the cavity when supine is posterior).

structures.name: Thickened apical pleura and adhesions
structures.note: Dense, vascular adhesions to the apex and chest wall: extrapleural dissection is often needed.

structures.name: Cavities and bronchiectasis (TB-destroyed lung)
structures.note: Schematic: a lung destroyed by tuberculosis: cavities, bronchiectasis and fibrosis, with volume loss and pleural symphysis; a reservoir for infection and haemoptysis.

structures.name: Congenital lobar emphysema: over-distended left upper lobe
structures.note: Schematic: a ball-valve defect in the lobar bronchus (deficient cartilage) lets air in but not out; the lobe over-distends, compresses the lower lobe and pushes the mediastinum across.

structures.name: CPAM: air-filled cysts, left lower lobe
structures.note: Schematic: thin-walled cysts of a congenital pulmonary airway malformation (Stocker type 1: one or more cysts over 2 cm). They connect poorly with the airway and become infected.

structures.name: Thymoma (about 5 cm), anterior mediastinum
structures.note: Schematic: an encapsulated, lobulated thymoma arising in the thymus, behind the sternum and in front of the pericardium and great veins.

structures.name: Esophageal carcinoma, middle third (squamous)
structures.note: Schematic: a circumferential squamous cell carcinoma at the level of the carina and the left main bronchus: check the airway (bronchoscopy) before resection.

structures.name: Esophageal carcinoma, lower third
structures.note: Schematic: a lower-third tumour above the gastro-esophageal junction.

structures.name: Infected fluid (post-pneumonectomy empyema)
structures.note: Schematic: after pneumonectomy the space fills with serous fluid over weeks; infected, it becomes empyema. A falling fluid level, or a new air-fluid level, suggests a bronchopleural fistula.

structures.name: Right main bronchial stump
structures.note: The right main bronchus divided flush with the carina: a long stump pools secretions and is more prone to break down.

structures.name: Bronchopleural fistula
structures.note: A breakdown of the stump: the airway opens into the infected space. Fluid is coughed up and can spill into the remaining lung.

structures.name: Open window thoracostomy (Eloesser flap)
structures.note: Segments of two ribs removed over the dependent part of the cavity; the skin is sutured to the parietal pleura so the window stays open and drains.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi flap (to the stump)
structures.note: A pedicled muscle flap on the thoracodorsal vessels brought into the chest (through a window or a resected rib bed) to cover the closed stump and fill part of the space.

structures.name: Renal artery, left
structures.note: Schematic on this patient's aorta and kidney.

structures.name: Renal artery, right
structures.note: Schematic on this patient's aorta and kidney. The right renal artery passes behind the IVC.

structures.name: Coeliac trunk
structures.note: Schematic: from the front of the aorta at T12/L1, dividing into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries.

structures.name: Superior mesenteric artery
structures.note: Schematic: about 1 cm below the coeliac trunk, running down in front of the left renal vein and the uncinate process.

structures.name: Inferior mesenteric artery
structures.note: Schematic: from the left front of the aorta at L3, often patent into an aneurysm; its reimplantation is considered when pelvic perfusion is doubtful.

structures.name: Inferior vena cava (infrarenal)
structures.note: Schematic below the segmented IVC: to the right of the aorta, the confluence of the iliac veins at L5.

structures.name: Left renal vein (in front of the aorta)
structures.note: Crosses in front of the aorta just below the SMA, receiving the gonadal (below), adrenal (above) and lumbar veins on the left. It marks the upper limit of an infrarenal neck; dividing it near the IVC gives access to the juxtarenal aorta.

structures.name: Common iliac artery, left (schematic, below the scan)
structures.note: Below the lower edge of this CT: drawn to typical adult dimensions.

structures.name: Common femoral artery, left (schematic)
structures.note: Under the inguinal ligament at the mid-inguinal point, bifurcating into the superficial and profunda femoris arteries.

structures.name: Groin incision, left (vertical, over the femoral artery)
structures.note: Schematic (below this scan): a vertical incision over the femoral pulse, from above the inguinal ligament down over the femoral bifurcation.

structures.name: Common and external iliac veins, left (schematic)
structures.note: Behind and then medial to the arteries; the left common iliac vein crosses behind the right common iliac artery.

structures.name: Common femoral vein, left (schematic)
structures.note: Medial to the femoral artery in the femoral sheath (nerve, artery, vein, empty space, lymphatics: NAVEL from lateral to medial).

structures.name: Inguinal ligament, left (schematic)
structures.note: From the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle; the external iliac artery becomes the common femoral artery beneath it, at the mid-inguinal point.

structures.name: Common iliac artery, right (schematic, below the scan)
structures.note: Below the lower edge of this CT: drawn to typical adult dimensions.

structures.name: Common femoral artery, right (schematic)
structures.note: Under the inguinal ligament at the mid-inguinal point, bifurcating into the superficial and profunda femoris arteries.

structures.name: Groin incision, right (vertical, over the femoral artery)
structures.note: Schematic (below this scan): a vertical incision over the femoral pulse, from above the inguinal ligament down over the femoral bifurcation.

structures.name: Common and external iliac veins, right (schematic)
structures.note: Behind and then medial to the arteries; the left common iliac vein crosses behind the right common iliac artery.

structures.name: Common femoral vein, right (schematic)
structures.note: Medial to the femoral artery in the femoral sheath (nerve, artery, vein, empty space, lymphatics: NAVEL from lateral to medial).

structures.name: Inguinal ligament, right (schematic)
structures.note: From the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle; the external iliac artery becomes the common femoral artery beneath it, at the mid-inguinal point.

structures.name: Ureter, left (schematic)
structures.note: Down on the psoas, crossing in front of the iliac bifurcation into the pelvis. The limbs of an aortobifemoral graft are tunnelled BEHIND it.

structures.name: Ureter, right (schematic)
structures.note: Down on the psoas, crossing in front of the iliac bifurcation into the pelvis. The limbs of an aortobifemoral graft are tunnelled BEHIND it.

structures.name: Infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (6 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a fusiform aneurysm starting 1.5-2 cm below the lowest renal artery (a good neck), to the bifurcation.

structures.name: Juxtarenal aneurysm (no infrarenal neck)
structures.note: Schematic: the aneurysm begins at the renal arteries without involving them; there is no room for an infrarenal clamp.

structures.name: Suprarenal (pararenal/paravisceral) aneurysm
structures.note: Schematic: the aneurysm involves the renal artery origins and extends up to the SMA; the clamp goes above the coeliac trunk or between it and the SMA.

structures.name: Aorto-iliac occlusion (thrombus and calcified plaque)
structures.note: Schematic: the distal aorta and both common iliac arteries occluded (Leriche syndrome, TASC II D), the aorta blocked up to near the IMA.

structures.name: Collaterals around the occlusion
structures.note: Schematic: lumbar to iliolumbar and circumflex iliac, internal thoracic to inferior epigastric (Winslow pathway), SMA to IMA (arc of Riolan). Do not divide them carelessly.

structures.name: Tube graft (Dacron), infrarenal
structures.note: Sewn inside the opened sac, from the neck to the bifurcation (or a bifurcated graft to the iliacs), then the sac closed over it.

structures.name: Tube graft, anastomosis at the renal arteries
Graft with a bevelled proximal anastomosis incorporating the visceral and right renal origins; left renal side-arm
structures.note: Schematic: the proximal suture line is bevelled to include the SMA and right renal origins as a patch; the left renal artery is reimplanted or bypassed with a side-arm.

structures.name: Bifurcated stent graft (EVAR)
structures.note: Schematic: sealing in the infrarenal neck (at least 10-15 mm of healthy, parallel aorta) and in both common iliac arteries; the sac is excluded, not removed.

structures.name: Aortobifemoral bypass graft (bifurcated, crimped Dacron)
structures.note: End-to-side on the front of the infrarenal aorta below the left renal vein; a short body; each limb in a retroperitoneal tunnel on the front of the iliac arteries, behind the ureter, under the inguinal ligament, end-to-side onto the common femoral artery.

structures.name: Kissing stents at the aortic bifurcation (covered, balloon-expandable)
structures.note: Two balloon-expandable covered stents side by side from the distal aorta into both common iliac arteries, their tops level about 1 cm above the old bifurcation (the new carina), inflated together.

structures.name: Two balloons inflated together (kissing inflation)
structures.note: Simultaneous inflation so that neither stent crushes the other at the carina.

structures.name: Axillary artery, right (first part medial to pectoralis minor)
structures.note: Schematic continuation of the subclavian from the outer border of the first rib; its first part, behind the clavipectoral fascia, takes the graft.

structures.name: Axillobifemoral bypass (8 mm ringed PTFE), with a femorofemoral cross-over
structures.note: Extra-anatomic: end-to-side on the first part of the axillary artery, running along it before turning down, subcutaneous in the mid-axillary line outside the ribs, in front of the iliac crest to the right groin; a suprapubic subcutaneous femorofemoral limb to the left groin.

structures.name: Suture lines: axillary and both femoral anastomoses
Left flank incision (retroperitoneal approach, through the 11th rib bed)
structures.note: From the tip of the 11th rib posteriorly, obliquely down to the lateral edge of the rectus sheath; the peritoneum and the left kidney swept forward (or the kidney left behind).

structures.name: Descending thoracic aortic aneurysm (6.4 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a fusiform aneurysm of the mid-descending thoracic aorta, beginning several centimetres beyond the left subclavian artery.

structures.name: Thoracic stent graft (TEVAR)
structures.note: Schematic: at least 20 mm of healthy aorta above and below (the landing zones); the sac excluded.

structures.name: Left intercostal artery and the artery of Adamkiewicz (arteria radicularis magna)
structures.note: Schematic: most often from a left intercostal artery between T9 and T12; it joins the anterior spinal artery with a hairpin turn and is the main supply to the lower cord.

structures.name: Lumbar CSF drain (L2-L3 or L3-L4)
structures.note: Drains CSF to keep the pressure at about 10-12 mmHg (not higher than 15), raising spinal cord perfusion pressure (MAP minus CSF pressure).

structures.name: Ascending aortic aneurysm (5.6 cm)
structures.note: Schematic: a supracoronary ascending aneurysm with a normal root and sinotubular junction, ending at the innominate artery.

structures.name: Aorta above the infrarenal neck
structures.note: The aorta from the CT, the diseased segment removed (it is drawn separately).

structures.name: Aorta above the renal arteries
structures.note: The aorta from the CT, the diseased segment removed (it is drawn separately).

structures.name: Aorta above the visceral segment
structures.note: The aorta from the CT, the diseased segment removed (it is drawn separately).

structures.name: Aorta with the aneurysmal descending segment removed
structures.note: The aorta from the CT, the diseased segment removed (it is drawn separately).

structures.name: Aorta with the ascending segment removed
structures.note: The aorta from the CT, the diseased segment removed (it is drawn separately).

structures.name: Aneurysm sac, opened longitudinally
structures.note: The front of the sac opened (to the right of the IMA), the thrombus scooped out; the walls fall back and later close over the graft.

structures.name: Laminated mural thrombus in the sac
structures.note: Layers of old thrombus line most aneurysms, leaving a channel of normal calibre: the sac is far larger than the lumen seen on angiography.

structures.name: Lumbar arteries (back-bleeding into the opened sac)
structures.note: Paired from the back of the aorta; after the sac is opened they are oversewn from inside with figure-of-eight sutures.

structures.name: Suture lines: proximal (neck) and distal (bifurcation) anastomoses
structures.note: Running 3-0 polypropylene, the back wall first from inside the sac, taking the full thickness of the aorta (and a strip of felt if it is friable).

structures.name: Suture line at the renal arteries
Suture lines: aortic (end-to-side) and both femoral anastomoses
Suture lines: proximal and distal thoracic anastomoses
Stiff guidewires and sheaths (both femoral arteries)
structures.note: Percutaneous (pre-closure sutures) or open femoral access; stiff wires up to the thoracic aorta; the main body travels up the ipsilateral side, the contralateral limb through a gate cannulated from the other groin.

structures.name: Stiff guidewire and sheath (right femoral) to the arch
Sheaths in both femorals; guidewires crossing both iliac occlusions
Thickened pericardium (constrictive, about 5–6 mm)
structures.note: Tuberculous constriction: a thick, fibrous, often calcified pericardium encases the heart and limits diastolic filling of all four chambers.

structures.name: Pericardial calcification
structures.note: Calcium is seen in about a quarter to a half of chronic constriction, typically over the atrioventricular grooves and the diaphragmatic surface: it marks the plane that is hardest to free.

structures.name: Pericardium remaining after phrenic-to-phrenic pericardiectomy
structures.note: Total (radical) pericardiectomy removes the pericardium from phrenic nerve to phrenic nerve, the diaphragmatic surface and over the cavae; a pedicle of pericardium is left with each phrenic nerve.

structures.name: Tibia, right (schematic)
structures.note: Subcutaneous medial surface and anterior crest: the landmarks for fasciotomy and below-knee amputation.

structures.name: Superficial femoral artery, right (to the adductor hiatus) (schematic)
Posterior tibial artery (behind the medial malleolus) (schematic)
Great saphenous vein (schematic)
structures.note: From the saphenofemoral junction (about 3 cm below and lateral to the pubic tubercle) down the medial thigh, behind the medial femoral condyle, to in front of the medial malleolus. The best conduit for infrainguinal bypass.

structures.name: Embolus at the femoral bifurcation (saddle)
structures.note: An embolus lodges where the artery divides and narrows: the common femoral bifurcation is the commonest site in the leg.

structures.name: Fogarty balloon catheter (4F) passed down to the trifurcation
structures.note: Passed beyond the clot, the balloon inflated gently with saline and withdrawn steadily, pulling the clot out of the arteriotomy; repeated until two clean passes and good back-bleeding.

structures.name: Anterior compartment (tibialis anterior; deep peroneal nerve, anterior tibial artery)
Deep posterior compartment (tibialis posterior, long flexors; tibial nerve, posterior tibial and peroneal vessels)
Anterolateral fasciotomy incision (anterior and lateral compartments)
structures.note: Midway between the tibial crest and the fibula, over the septum between the anterior and lateral compartments; protect the superficial peroneal nerve in the lower third.

structures.name: Posteromedial fasciotomy incision (superficial and deep posterior compartments)
structures.note: 1–2 cm behind the posteromedial border of the tibia; protect the great saphenous vein and saphenous nerve; detach soleus from the tibia to reach the deep compartment.

structures.name: Superficial femoral artery occlusion (atherosclerotic, about 20 cm)
structures.note: The commonest site of lower limb occlusive disease, at the adductor canal; collaterals from the profunda reconstitute the popliteal.

structures.name: Reversed great saphenous vein graft: common femoral to below-knee popliteal
structures.note: Reversed so that its valves do not obstruct flow; tunnelled deep to sartorius and behind the knee; end-to-side at both ends.

structures.name: Suture lines: femoral and below-knee popliteal anastomoses
Incisions over the saphenous vein (harvest) and the below-knee popliteal
Above-knee amputation level (mid-thigh; equal anterior and posterior flaps)
Below-knee amputation level (about 12–15 cm below the knee joint; long posterior flap)
Long posterior myocutaneous flap (Burgess)
structures.note: The anterior incision at the level of bone section; a posterior flap about as long as the leg is wide at that level, folded forward over the bone end.

structures.name: Skin of the right arm and forearm (forearm schematic)
Brachial artery (medial to the humerus; medial to the biceps tendon at the elbow)
Cephalic vein (radial side; lateral arm; deltopectoral groove)
Basilic vein (ulnar side; deep to the fascia in the upper arm)
Radiocephalic fistula (Brescia–Cimino): cephalic vein end-to-side to the radial artery
Matured forearm cephalic vein (about 6 mm, superficial)
Brachiocephalic fistula: cephalic vein (or median cubital) to the brachial artery at the elbow
Matured cephalic vein in the upper arm
Transposed brachiobasilic fistula: the basilic vein brought to the surface
structures.note: The basilic vein is deep and medial, beside the median and medial cutaneous nerves: mobilised along the arm and tunnelled superficially and laterally so it can be needled.

structures.name: Incisions: longitudinal at the wrist; transverse in the antecubital fossa; medial arm (basilic transposition)
Bronchiectasis: dilated, varicose and cystic bronchi (left upper lobe)
structures.note: Traction and post-infective bronchiectasis after tuberculosis: thick-walled, dilated bronchi pooling secretions, with recurrent infection and haemoptysis.

structures.name: Hypertrophied, tortuous bronchial artery (the source of haemoptysis)
structures.note: Chronic inflammation enlarges the bronchial arteries (systemic pressure): they bleed into the bronchi. Bronchial artery embolisation is the first treatment for massive haemoptysis; surgery removes the source.

structures.name: Dense pleural adhesions (pleural symphysis)
structures.note: After tuberculosis the lung is often fused to the chest wall: an extrapleural plane may be safer than fighting through the adhesions.

structures.name: Secundum atrial septal defect (fossa ovalis, about 18 mm)
structures.note: Schematic. A deficiency of the floor of the fossa ovalis (septum primum). The rim: superior toward the SVC and aorta, inferior toward the IVC, posterior toward the right pulmonary veins.

structures.name: Left-to-right shunt across the ASD (mostly in late diastole)
structures.note: Schematic. Flow follows the compliance of the ventricles: the thinner, more compliant RV fills preferentially, so blood crosses from LA to RA.

structures.name: Autologous pericardial patch (ASD closure)
structures.note: Schematic. Fresh or glutaraldehyde-treated autologous pericardium, sewn to the rim with running 5-0 polypropylene; small defects may be closed directly.

structures.name: Superior sinus venosus defect: at the SVC entry, with the right upper pulmonary vein draining anomalously
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this ASD type.

structures.name: Inferior sinus venosus defect: at the IVC entry
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this ASD type.

structures.name: Ostium primum defect: low, just above the AV valves (a partial AV septal defect)
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this ASD type.

structures.name: Coronary sinus (unroofed) defect: at the coronary sinus orifice
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this ASD type.

structures.name: Perimembranous ventricular septal defect (about 10 mm)
structures.note: Schematic. In the membranous septum, below the right and non-coronary cusps, partly under the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve. The His bundle runs along its posteroinferior rim.

structures.name: Left-to-right shunt across the VSD (systole)
structures.note: Schematic. LV systolic pressure drives flow into the RV and on to the lungs: the LA and LV take the volume load.

structures.name: Dacron patch (VSD closure)
structures.note: Schematic. Dacron, PTFE or treated pericardium, on the RV side, with interrupted pledgeted or running 5-0/6-0 polypropylene.

structures.name: Suture line: shallow bites on the RV side of the posteroinferior rim
Type 1, subarterial (outlet, doubly committed): under the pulmonary and aortic valves
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this type (STS / Congenital Heart Surgery Nomenclature types 1 to 4 and the Gerbode defect).

structures.name: Type 3, inlet (AV canal type): under the septal tricuspid leaflet, behind the perimembranous zone
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this type (STS / Congenital Heart Surgery Nomenclature types 1 to 4 and the Gerbode defect).

structures.name: Type 4, muscular (trabecular): surrounded by muscle; mid, apical, anterior or posterior; often multiple
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this type (STS / Congenital Heart Surgery Nomenclature types 1 to 4 and the Gerbode defect).

structures.name: Gerbode defect: left ventricle to right atrium, through the atrioventricular membranous septum
structures.note: Schematic marker of the typical position of this type (STS / Congenital Heart Surgery Nomenclature types 1 to 4 and the Gerbode defect).

structures.name: Patent ductus arteriosus (about 8 mm)
structures.note: Schematic. From the concavity of the arch at the isthmus, opposite the left subclavian origin, to the top of the left pulmonary artery near its origin. The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under it.

structures.name: Two heavy ligatures (aortic end first)
structures.note: Schematic. Non-absorbable (e.g. 2-0 or heavier braided) ligatures; aortic end first. A clip suits small infants; division between clamps suits a short, wide or older duct.

structures.name: Titanium clip across the ductus (infant alternative)
Type A, conical
structures.note: Schematic specimen (Krichenko angiographic classification, lateral view): aorta above, pulmonary artery below.

structures.name: Type B, window
structures.note: Schematic specimen (Krichenko angiographic classification, lateral view): aorta above, pulmonary artery below.

structures.name: Type C, tubular
structures.note: Schematic specimen (Krichenko angiographic classification, lateral view): aorta above, pulmonary artery below.

structures.name: Type D, complex
structures.note: Schematic specimen (Krichenko angiographic classification, lateral view): aorta above, pulmonary artery below.

structures.name: Type E, elongated
structures.note: Schematic specimen (Krichenko angiographic classification, lateral view): aorta above, pulmonary artery below.

structures.name: Coarctation of the aorta: juxtaductal shelf, post-stenotic dilatation
structures.note: Schematic. A posterior shelf of thickened media and intima at the isthmus, opposite the duct; the lumen here is a third of normal. The aorta dilates beyond it.

structures.name: Coarctation shelf (ridge of intima and media)
Descending aorta after resection and extended end-to-end anastomosis
structures.note: Schematic. The narrowed segment and ductal tissue excised; the descending aorta brought up to an incision extended along the underside of the arch.

structures.name: Anastomosis: running polypropylene (oblique, extended under the arch)
Enlarged, tortuous intercostal collaterals
structures.note: Schematic. Collaterals from the subclavian branches (internal thoracic, thyrocervical) fill the intercostals, which run backwards into the aorta below the coarctation. They cause rib notching and bleed when the chest is opened.

structures.name: Clamps: distal arch (with the subclavian origin) and descending aorta
structures.note: Schematic. Proximal clamp across the distal arch beyond the left carotid, including the subclavian origin; distal clamp on the descending aorta below the intercostals that have been controlled.

structures.name: Malalignment VSD (large, subaortic, non-restrictive)
structures.note: Schematic. Anterior and cephalad deviation of the outlet septum leaves a large defect under the aorta; the aorta straddles it.

structures.name: RV blood ejected into the overriding aorta (right-to-left)
structures.note: Schematic. With a non-restrictive VSD and RVOT obstruction, desaturated RV blood goes to the aorta: cyanosis.

structures.name: Infundibular stenosis: hypertrophied septoparietal muscle bands
structures.note: Schematic. The deviated outlet septum and hypertrophied trabeculations narrow the RV outflow below the valve; this is the dynamic part that spasms in a tet spell.

structures.name: Small, thickened pulmonary valve and annulus
structures.note: Schematic. Often bicuspid and stenotic; the annulus z-score decides whether it can be kept.

structures.name: Muscle resected from the RV outflow
VSD patch (closes the VSD, baffling LV to aorta)
Transannular patch (RV outflow, across the annulus, onto the trunk)
structures.note: Schematic. Autologous pericardium across the opened annulus when it is too small; relieves obstruction at the cost of free pulmonary regurgitation.

structures.name: Incision: infundibulum, across the annulus, onto the trunk
Modified Blalock-Taussig shunt (PTFE, 3.5–4 mm): innominate artery to right PA
structures.note: Schematic. Gore-Tex tube from the distal innominate (or subclavian) artery to the top of the ipsilateral pulmonary artery.

structures.name: Pulmonary artery band (Teflon or PTFE tape) on the main trunk
structures.note: Schematic. Placed on the main trunk clear of the valve below and the branches above; tightened to a circumference by Trusler's rule and by distal PA pressure.

structures.name: Left posterolateral thoracotomy, 3rd intercostal space
structures.note: Schematic: along the 3rd space, from below the axilla, round the tip of the scapula to the paraspinal muscles. Higher: straight onto the distal arch, the subclavian and the duct; cramped under the scapula in a bigger child.

structures.name: Left posterolateral thoracotomy, 4th intercostal space
structures.note: Schematic: along the 4th space, from below the axilla, round the tip of the scapula to the paraspinal muscles. The standard space: the isthmus and the duct lie at its level, with room to reach the arch above and the descending aorta below.

structures.name: Anastomotic defect (intrathoracic)
structures.note: Schematic: a full-thickness defect in the right posterior wall of the intrathoracic anastomosis. Size it at endoscopy as a fraction of the circumference.

structures.name: Mediastinal collection
structures.note: Schematic: saliva, gastric juice and pus tracking beside the conduit in the posterior mediastinum.

structures.name: Right pleural collection (empyema)
structures.note: Schematic: the leak has broken into the right pleural space: a layering, infected effusion.

structures.name: Chest drain (right)
structures.note: Schematic: image-guided or surgical tube drainage of the pleural collection, its tip toward the mediastinal leak.

structures.name: Nasogastric tube (conduit decompression)
structures.note: Schematic: placed under vision past the anastomosis to decompress the conduit. Never passed blind after an esophagectomy.

structures.name: Endoscopic vacuum sponge (EVT)
structures.note: Schematic: open-pore polyurethane sponge on a drainage tube, placed endoscopically through the defect into the cavity (intracavitary) or across it in the lumen (intraluminal); continuous suction -100 to -125 mmHg, changed every 3-4 days.

structures.name: EVT suction tube (out through the nose)
structures.note: Schematic: the sponge's tube leaves through the nose to a continuous suction unit.

structures.name: Fully covered self-expanding metal stent
structures.note: Schematic: a fully covered stent bridging the anastomosis, about 4 cm either side of the defect. Usually removed or exchanged by 4-8 weeks.

structures.name: Cervical leak: collection under the neck wound
structures.note: Schematic: saliva and pus beside the cervical anastomosis, deep to the sternocleidomastoid.

structures.name: Neck wound opened and packed
structures.note: Schematic: the incision opened at the bedside, the space drained and packed with gauze.

structures.name: Necrosis of the conduit tip
structures.note: Schematic: the ischemic tip of the gastric conduit, the part farthest from its blood supply. Limited: continuity-preserving treatment; extensive: resection and diversion.

structures.name: Cervical esophagostomy (spit fistula)
structures.note: Schematic: after the conduit is taken down, the esophageal remnant is brought out on the left neck so saliva drains to a bag.

structures.name: Common iliac artery aneurysm, right (42 mm)
structures.note: Schematic: a fusiform 4.2 cm aneurysm of the right common iliac artery, the whole length from the aortic bifurcation to the iliac bifurcation. Repair threshold 40 mm (ESVS 2024).

structures.name: Mural thrombus in the iliac aneurysm
Iliac branch device, right (with a covered bridging stent into the internal iliac)
structures.note: Schematic: the iliac branch device lands in the external iliac artery; its side branch is bridged into the internal iliac artery with a covered stent, so pelvic flow is preserved. Joined to a standard bifurcated EVAR.

structures.name: Coils in the right internal iliac artery
structures.note: Schematic: the internal iliac origin is embolised so the limb can be extended into the external iliac without a type II endoleak from the pelvis. Buttock claudication follows in a quarter to a third.

structures.name: EVAR limb extended into the right external iliac
Open repair: interposition graft, right common iliac, internal iliac re-implanted
structures.note: Schematic: through a retroperitoneal or midline approach, a 10-12 mm Dacron graft from the aortic bifurcation to the external iliac origin, with a side limb (or the native vessel) to the internal iliac.

structures.name: Blood pressure cuff above the ankle
structures.note: Schematic: a 12 cm cuff just above the malleoli; inflate until the Doppler signal goes, deflate until it returns.

structures.name: Hand-held Doppler probe on the dorsalis pedis
structures.note: 8 MHz pencil probe at 45-60 degrees to the artery, with gel; repeat on the posterior tibial behind the medial malleolus.

structures.name: Blood pressure cuff on the upper arm
structures.note: Schematic: brachial systolic pressure by Doppler in both arms; use the higher of the two.

source.name: Reference CT: 3D Slicer sample CTA (CTA-cardio)
source.note: Segmented with TotalSegmentator (total and lung_vessels). Branch names are assigned from the geometry of this one scan and need a surgeon's check.
